author: Inside Edition
description: Dozens of teens gathered on the front porch of their high school principal Brian Muller in the early morning hours. The principal got quite the wake up call. He walked out of his room to find the large group of students sitting in his home. Turns out, it was a senior prank. Seniors Dash Stoltz and Jayden Batts-Finch of Northwest Guilford High School in Greensboro, North Carolina, were the brains behind the operation. With a little help from Principal Muller's wife, the plan was a go. The principal spoke with Inside Edition.
title: Students Gather Inside High School Principal's Home In Senior Prank

author: Inside Edition
description: A little girl was preparing to take a jump at an indoor fun park when she crash landed on the mat below. 8-year-old Vivian Huber broke her leg. The child and her mother, Jennifer, spoke with Inside Edition's Les Trent. This is not the first time an accident happened at the adventure park, Spy Ninjas HQ in Las Vegas. In February, 10-year-old Knox Hill fell more than 20 feet from a zipline despite being harnessed. He suffered a concussion. Spy Ninjas HQ tells Inside Edition the health and safety of its guests is one of its top priorities, and that at the time of Huber's incident, no medical services were requested or deemed necessary by her guardian. Apy Ninjas HQ also tells Inside Edition they wish her a swift recovery.
title: 8-Year-Old Girl Breaks Her Leg At Indoor Fun Park

author: Inside Edition
description: Les Trent has called Inside Edition home for 26 years. He has brought the world into living rooms and has covered the biggest newsmakers. When a murderous gunman targeted a supermarket in his beloved hometown of Buffalo, New York, the mayor thanked Trent personally. Trent had a special knack for making people he encountered feel comfortable. Inside Edition says thank you and farewell to a devoted member of the Inside Edition family.
title: Les Trent Retires After 26 Years With Inside Edition

author: Inside Edition
description: It seems scientists are looking to recycle anything these days. A group of them in the UK are currently experimenting with making fertilizer, not from using number two, but from number one. They call it pee-cycling. They've been collecting as much of the liquid waste as they can from big events like festivals and races. The company, NPK Recovery, calls it circular sanitation. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Scientists Turn Urine Into Fertilizer By Pee-cycling

author: Inside Edition
description: Does this buffalo remind you of someone? Fans in Bangladesh see the resemblance. Its fluffy blonde coif has earned it the nickname Donald Trump. This 1,500 pound buffalo is special for another reason - it's albino, which is rare in the country. The animal's owner says it is a gentle creature, but requires a lot of maintenance like continued feeding. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Viral Albino Buffalo With Trump-like Hair Spared From Ritual Sacrifice
